newsitem.title: UK: Most Britons support ban on landmines - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Britons support ban on landmines - poll.

text.p: Ninety percent of Britons agree with Princess Diana and want an international ban on anti-personnel mines, according to a poll released on Wednesday.

The poll commissioned by six British aid agencies showed the overwhelming majority of the 1,001 people interviewed supported Diana's view on the sensitive issue which seemed to be at odds with government policy.
The aid agencies accused the British government of "double-speak" for its statements on anti-personnel mines.

"The government trumpets well meaning words while pursuing a policy that will set back a global ban by 10 years. That delay could cost the lives and limbs of up to 250,000 people," Tim Carstairs, co-ordinator of the UK Working Group on Landmines, said in a statement.
Diana's comments during a Red Cross trip to Angola caused a political storm in Britain where a minister called her remarks "very uninformed."
Britain backs a ban on most anti-personnel mines but says it must be international to be effective. So-called "smart mines" that self-destruct after a period of time are excluded.

"In short, the government's diplomacy is in stark contrast to the wishes of the overwhelming majority of the British public and shames us all. There is no better time than now for the government to ban these evil weapons," Carstairs added.

Oxfam UK and Ireland, Save the Children (UK), Christian Aid, the Catholic charity CAFORD, Mines Advisory Group and Medecins sans Frontieres (UK) which commissioned the poll are members of the UK Working Group on Landmines.
